notes:
Account summary
- High-throughput embeddings workload (primary). Mix of: (1) online semantic search for operator-assist UI, (2) nightly ingest backfills when new manuals / tickets land, (3) occasional re-embedding during model upgrades.
- Latency-sensitive for online path: they care about p95 end-to-end < 250ms (their app budget). They said: "If p95 drifts, search feels broken and the operators stop trusting it."

PLG context / why this got routed
- Product-led signal flagged due to sustained spend velocity (not a one-day spike) + repeated near-capacity behavior.
- Some 429s during ingest windows; customer said they can retry but it drags batch jobs into business hours.

Current setup (customer-reported)
- Using Hosted API today for embeddings; they batch some requests but still see burstiness.
- Regions: currently US-only; asked if we can support a second region later for redundancy (not immediate).
- Wants predictability: prefers a known baseline capacity and controlled burst, rather than pure best-effort.

What they’re evaluating
- Dedicated capacity to stabilize throughput/latency and avoid 429s during batch ingest.
- Interested in Redwood Optimize guidance for batching/caching + quantization recommendations (but first priority is Dedicated baseline).

POC milestones (draft / agreed on call 2025-05-22)
1) Benchmark: run their representative payloads on two configs (A100 vs H100 pool) with target p95 + throughput (owner: Markus).
2) Capacity sizing: propose baseline GPUs + burst policy for ingest windows; include expected cost per 1M embeddings (owner: Markus + Stephanie).
3) Integration: validate SDK changes minimal; confirm retry/backoff behavior and streaming not needed (owner: customer eng lead; Redwood to provide sample config).
4) Success criteria: p95 <= 250ms online path; ingest window completes within 3 hours; zero 429s in steady state.
5) Commercial: commit band + overage policy; request is to cap surprises and get predictable monthly spend.

Open questions
- Exact online QPS distribution (mean vs peak) still fuzzy; they gave partial numbers but not per-hour histogram.
- Embedding model preference: they’re currently on a general-purpose model; open to Redwood-recommended model if quality holds.
- Need to confirm if they require SSO for console access immediately or only later in procurement.

Internal notes
- This is a good fit for Dedicated rather than Private right now (no strict VPC requirement stated; more performance/cost predictability).
- Keep outreach tight (customer sensitive to spam; came in via PLG). Coordinate touches with marketing nurture to avoid duplicates.
